facts.d: Ladakh is larger than most Indian states in area, with a population of about 2.74 lakh, and sends a single member to the Lok Sabha. It has no legislative assembly at all — every law applying to it is made by Parliament or by executive order.

facts.t: The Sixth Schedule was written for the North-East
facts.d: Articles 244(2) and 275(1) apply it to tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Extending it to a Himalayan border territory would require a constitutional amendment — one reason the demand has been so hard to satisfy.

facts.t: Leh and Kargil want protection, but not the same protection
facts.d: Kargil is Muslim-majority and Leh Buddhist-majority, and the two Hill Councils have differed on whether statehood or Sixth Schedule status should come first. That internal divergence is as significant an obstacle as anything in Delhi.

bank.q: With reference to Ladakh's present constitutional position, consider the following statements:
s: It is administered by a Lieutenant Governor with no elected legislative assembly.
The Autonomous Hill Development Councils of Leh and Kargil are its only elected bodies.
It has two Lok Sabha constituencies.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Ladakh has a single Lok Sabha seat for the entire Union Territory — more representation is one of the four core demands.

bank.q: The Sixth Schedule currently applies to tribal areas in:
o: Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Tripura and Sikkim
bank.e: Those four states, under Articles 244(2) and 275(1). Extension elsewhere requires a constitutional amendment.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the four principal demands from Ladakh?
o: Full statehood with its own legislature
A separate High Court for Ladakh
A separate Public Service Commission and local job reservation
bank.e: A separate High Court is not among them. The fourth demand is greater Lok Sabha representation.

bank.q: Consider the following powers of Autonomous District Councils under the Sixth Schedule:
s: Legislating on land, forests other than reserved forests, and jhum cultivation.
Running village courts applying customary law.
bank.e: All three are correct, along with regulating money-lending and trading by non-tribals and managing schools, dispensaries, markets and ferries.

bank.as: The abrogation of Article 35A intensified Ladakhi anxieties about land.
bank.rs: It removed the State Subject protection that had barred outsiders from purchasing land.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. Fear of demographic influx in an ecologically fragile, pastoral economy is the core of the Sixth Schedule demand.

bank.q: All of the following are cited as obstacles to extending the Sixth Schedule to Ladakh EXCEPT:
o: Its status as a strategic border territory in a live conflict zone
The precedent it would set for other Union Territories
The absence of any tribal population in the region
Complexity in dividing powers between the Council, the Lieutenant Governor and Parliament
bank.e: Ladakh has a substantial tribal population — that is the basis of the demand, not an obstacle to it.

bank.q: Match List I (proposed measure) with List II (time horizon):
pairs: A. Amending the LAHDC Act to strengthen Hill Councils
C. A Ladakh-specific schedule analogous to Article 371
D. Reviving time-bound High-Powered Committee talks
bank.e: Statutory strengthening of the Councils is the short-term measure, statehood the medium-term one, a bespoke schedule the constitutional route, and reviving dialogue the process measure.

bank.q: The Autonomous Hill Development Councils of Leh and Kargil were established under an Act of:
bank.e: The LAHDC Act of 1997. Their functions and funds were squeezed after 2019 by the Lieutenant Governor's authority.

bank.q: Consider the following reasons advanced for Sixth Schedule protection in Ladakh:
s: Ecological fragility of glaciers, pastures and wetlands tied to tribal land use.
Survival of the Ladakhi, Balti and Purgi languages and of Buddhist and Shia customs.
The Hill Councils gained substantial new powers after 2019.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Councils were diluted rather than strengthened after 2019 — funds, functions and functionaries were squeezed.

bank.q: Which existing constitutional device is suggested as a model for a Ladakh-specific arrangement?
bank.e: Article 371 and its variants, which provide bespoke special provisions for particular states without extending a general schedule.
